title: Read-only Claude delegations refuse an informational `engram … --help`, so a reviewer cannot check a command's real CLI help
outcome: A read-only Claude delegation may run the informational help of known project CLIs (at least the Engram CLI, e.g. `engram.exe <subcommand…> --help` or `help`), recognized narrowly so that only a help request with no other effect is admitted; every other invocation of those executables stays refused. The Codex and Claude read-only reviewers can then make the same runtime-help observation.
acceptance: A read-only Claude delegation's Bash gate admits only a single informational Engram help invocation whose absolute executable identity matches the resolved host-controlled configured Engram binary path. It admits root --help/-h, supported literal subcommand paths ending in --help/-h, and the CLI's supported help-subcommand forms. Reviewer-controlled basename/PATH resolution never supplies the trusted identity; the allowed command is preserved unchanged and its help output can reach the reviewer.

Every other Engram invocation stays refused with the existing read-only message, including a command without help, help combined with other options or unproved extra arguments, an untrusted executable (including another file named engram.exe), relative/bare executable invocation, and help composed with shell chaining, pipes, redirection or wrappers. There is no general <any executable> --help allowance; existing read-only command behavior is unchanged.

Tests cover admitted and refused forms through the production host permission seam, including host configuration changes, quoted Windows absolute and Git Bash executable spellings, preserved permission input and existing read-only allowlist controls. The maintained full gate passes on the exact final input.
